max_tire.note: The Unlimited Rubicon came with ≈31-inch 245/75R16s from the factory. Use wheels with at least 4.5 in of backspacing.
Quadratec's guide for TJ/LJ: about 31 in on a 2 in spacer lift.
Quadratec's guide: 33 in on a 3 in suspension lift, 35 in with a long-arm lift. The low-hanging fuel tank is worth a skid plate.

items.title: 42RLE park pawl anchor shaft
items.summary: An improperly installed cup plug can let the shaft move so the transmission won't go into Park; dealers added a retaining bracket.

items.title: Six-speed clutch master cylinder rod
items.summary: The linkage rod can break so the clutch won't disengage; replaced free.

items.title: Clutch pedal interlock switch
items.summary: Switch springs can break, letting the engine start in gear without the clutch pressed; switch replaced free.

timeline.change: Wrangler Unlimited launches in April 2004 (the 2004½ model): 103.4-inch wheelbase (10 in longer than a TJ), one extra frame crossmember, standard Dana 44 rear with 3.73 gears, NV231 transfer case and 3,500 lb towing
Unlimited Rubicon arrives with front and rear locking Dana 44s, the Rock-Trac NV241OR and 245/75R16 MT/Rs; NSG370 six-speed replaces the five-speed manual
Sahara Edition Unlimited Rubicon: 1,000 numbered trucks, all Light Khaki
Final year; production ends in July 2006 and the four-door JK Unlimited takes over for 2007

identify.intro: "LJ" is an unofficial nickname. Jeep sold it as the Wrangler Unlimited, so the VIN, the wheelbase and the axles are how you tell one apart, and how you spot a stretched TJ or a Sport wearing Rubicon parts.

items.head: VIN
items.body: In the VINs we decoded with NHTSA's tool, an Unlimited reads 1J4FA44S… and an Unlimited Rubicon 1J4FA64S…. Short-wheelbase trucks have a 9 as the 7th character (1J4FA49S Sport, 1J4FA69S Rubicon).

items.head: Wheelbase and length
items.body: 103.4 in wheelbase against 93.4 in for a TJ, and about 167 in long to the bumper. The rear doors aren't there, but the long rear quarters and cargo area are hard to miss.

items.head: Rubicon hardware
items.body: Unlimited Rubicons have front and rear Dana 44s with lockers, the NV241OR (4:1 low range), diamond-plate rocker guards and 245/75R16 tires. Base Unlimiteds have a Dana 30 front, Dana 44 rear and the NV231 (2.72:1 low).

items.head: Sahara Edition
items.body: The 2005 Sahara Edition Unlimited Rubicon is Light Khaki with a numbered dash badge, chrome grille and Sahara spare-tire cover.

values.intro: The LJ sells for more than a comparable TJ: a one-generation long-wheelbase body plus the Rubicon spec make clean ones scarce, and good Unlimited Rubicons are near the top of the TJ market.
values.note: Based on 55 Unlimited sales on Bring a Trailer from April 2025 to October 2026: median ≈$20,500, middle half ≈$16,000–27,250. Unlimited Rubicons had a median of ≈$25,250, topping out around $37,000–38,000 (a 33k-mile 2005 Rubicon and a Vortec-swapped 2005 Rubicon).
